A.P. Moller - Maersk reported a group ROIC of 12.3% for 2024.

- This was above the yearly target of above 7.5% under normalised conditions; profitability lagged in the first half of 2024, but the strong second-half result brought ROIC above target (Roadmap towards 2025).
- The average ROIC over 2021-2024 was 31.3%, well above the 12% target for 2021-2025 (Roadmap towards 2025).
- ROIC is defined as profit/loss before financial items for the year (EBIT) less tax on EBIT, divided by the average invested capital over the last twelve months (Definition of terms).

ArcelorMittal reported a group-wide LTIFR of 0.70 for 2024. The glossary defines LTIFR as Lost Time Injuries per 1,000,000 worked hours (own personnel and contractors). A lost time injury (LTI) is an incident that causes an injury preventing the person from returning to his/her next scheduled shift or work period. The 0.70 figure appears in the Sustainable development section's 2024 performance disclosure and the segment table (Total LTIFR 2024).

Lerøy Havfisk's catch volume fell from 75 893 tonnes in 2023 to 64 991 tonnes in 2024 (a decrease of 10 902 tonnes, or roughly 14%).

- The fall reflects significant quota cuts: cod quotas were reduced by 34% and haddock by 43% year-on-year, plus a 6% reduction in the saithe quota in the northern zone (Results – Group, [1][2]).
- The quota reduction is only partly offset by higher prices, which help the trawler fleet but challenge the land-based industry; onshore whitefish processing made another loss in 2024, larger than in 2023 (Results – Group, [2]).
- On the outlook, the company says earnings in the WildCatch segment have been significantly affected by the low quota basis and will remain so for some time, with 2025 and probably also 2026 expected to be challenging for the segment (Results – Group / Market and outlook, [3][6]).
- Strategically, quotas for the highest-value species, cod, will fall further in 2025, so Lerøy aims to maintain efficient WildCatch operations while increasing onshore capacity utilisation by scaling up new processed products (Strategic priorities – WildCatch, [4]).

Mowi - 2024: 501 530 tonnes gutted weight of salmon
Lerøy Seafood Group - 2024: about 171 000 GWT of salmon and trout

Mowi harvested roughly 330 000 tonnes more than Lerøy in 2024 (501 530 vs. 171 000 GWT), nearly three times Lerøy's volume. Note Lerøy's figure includes trout, so the salmon-only comparison is not exact.

ArcelorMittal - calendar 2024: 57.9 million tonnes
Tata Steel Group - FY2023-24: 29.94 MT

ArcelorMittal's crude steel production was roughly 1.9 times larger (57.9 ÷ 29.94 ≈ 1.9). Note the periods differ (calendar year vs. fiscal year), so this is an approximate comparison.

A.P. Moller - Maersk - 2024: average number of employees 106,626
Rio Tinto - 2024: average number of employees 59,594

A.P. Moller - Maersk employed more people on average in 2024, by roughly 47,032 (106,626 − 59,594). Note the figures are not directly comparable: Maersk reports average headcount per month, while Rio Tinto's average includes proportional counts for joint operations and equity accounted units and FTE treatment of part-timers.

Mowi Norway - 2024 guidance (per 2023 report): 305k GWT
Mowi Norway - 2024 actual: 303 501 GWT (304k GWT)

The actual 2024 harvest of 303 501 GWT came within about 1 500 tonnes of the 305k GWT guidance, i.e. roughly 1.5k GWT (about 0.5%) below the guided volume.

ArcelorMittal Annual Report 2023 - expectation for 2024: between $0.3 to $0.4 billion (per [1]; another passage states $0.3-$0.6 billion net of government support per [4])
ArcelorMittal Annual Report 2024 - actual 2024 spend: $0.3 billion

ArcelorMittal expected 2024 decarbonization capital expenditures of $0.3 to $0.4 billion and actually spent $0.3 billion, at the lower end of the expected range.
